before.heading: Information we collect
before.body: We collect your name, email, account credentials, postal address, declared state of residence and saved events. We also collect device identifiers, approximate location and activity on our website.

after.heading: Information practices in the preceding 12 months
after.body:
During the 12 months before the proposed policy update, we collected the following categories. The same inventory describes the new California signup. A postal address, declared legal residence, and coarse device-derived location are different information; we do not treat an address or IP location alone as proof of legal residence. We do not collect precise device location. 

Identifiers. Examples: name, email, postal address, account ID, IP address. Sources: consumer directly, device interaction. Purposes: create and service account, deliver selected local event recommendations, security. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider, transactional email service provider. Retention: Account life plus 30 days after closure; security IP logs 90 days, subject to documented legal holds.

Personal information described in California Civil Code section 1798.80(e). Examples: name, postal address. Sources: consumer directly. Purposes: service account and user-selected region. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider. Retention: Account life plus 30 days after closure, subject to documented legal holds.

Internet or other electronic network activity information. Examples: event views, search activity. Sources: device interaction. Purposes: operate discovery, diagnose errors, improve first-party recommendations. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider, restricted first-party analytics service provider. Retention: 90 days, then deleted or deidentified; retained security incidents subject to documented legal hold.

Geolocation data. Examples: declared city, coarse IP-derived city. Sources: consumer directly, device interaction. Purposes: localize discovery. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider. Retention: Declared city for account life plus 30 days; coarse IP-derived location 90 days.

Inferences drawn from personal information. Examples: music interests inferred from saved event categories. Sources: derived from first-party interactions. Purposes: first-party event recommendations. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider. Retention: Until preferences reset or account closure plus 30 days.

Sensitive personal information: account login and access credentials. Examples: account login combined with access credentials. Sources: consumer directly. Purposes: authenticate requested account, protect account security. Business-purpose recipients in that period: authentication service provider. Retention: Until credential rotation or account closure; revocable session credentials expire within 30 days.

edits.rationale: map_inventory — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Sources of information
after.body: We collect account information, postal address, residence declarations, saved events and support messages directly from you. We collect identifiers, approximate location and usage information from your browser when you use our service. We derive music preferences from first-party interactions. We do not buy consumer information from data brokers.

edits.rationale: map_inventory — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

before.heading: How we use information
before.body: We use information to provide accounts, recommend local events, respond to support requests, and keep the service secure.

after.heading: Purposes for collection and use
after.body: We use information for the category-specific purposes stated above. We also use identifiers to respond to support and assess privacy requirements that may apply to your residence declaration. We do not use event recommendations to make decisions about financial or lending services, housing, insurance, education, employment or healthcare.

edits.rationale: map_inventory — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

before.heading: How we disclose information
before.body: We use providers to host the service, deliver email and help us understand first-party activity. We do not sell personal information.

after.heading: Disclosures for business purposes in the preceding 12 months
after.body: We disclosed each category listed in the information-practices section to its listed service-provider categories for the purposes stated there. These hosting, authentication, transactional email and restricted first-party analytics providers operate under contracts restricting their use to the permitted service. We have not otherwise disclosed these categories to third parties during the preceding 12 months.

edits.rationale: map_disclosures — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Sale or sharing of personal information
after.body: We have not sold personal information or shared it for cross-context behavioral advertising during the preceding 12 months, and we do not currently do either. We do not have actual knowledge that we sell or share personal information of consumers under 16. We do not use third-party advertising trackers or allow our providers to use consumer information for their own advertising.

edits.rationale: map_optout; map_supplement_third_party_advertising_trackers — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Sensitive personal information
after.body: We use and disclose account login credentials only as reasonably necessary to provide and secure the account service you request. We do not use or disclose sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those permitted by section 7027(m) of the California privacy regulations, and we do not use it to infer characteristics about you.

edits.rationale: map_sensitive_limit — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

before.heading: How long we keep information
before.body: We keep information for as long as we need it to provide our service and meet our obligations.

after.heading: Retention
after.body: The information-practices section states a period or criterion for each category. We keep support correspondence for 12 months after a request closes and records of privacy requests and our responses for at least 24 months. Documented legal holds may require limited information to be retained longer to meet a legal obligation, establish or defend a claim, or investigate a security incident. We restrict that information to the hold purpose and do not keep personal information longer than reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose.

edits.rationale: map_retention_notice; map_supplement_support_correspondence_retention_months — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: California privacy rights
after.body: California residents may ask us to know the personal information we have collected about them, including categories and specific pieces, sources, purposes, and categories of recipients; to delete personal information, subject to legal exceptions; and to correct inaccurate personal information. Where applicable, consumers may opt out of sale or sharing and limit certain uses or disclosures of sensitive personal information. Our current no-sale/no-sharing practices and limited account-security uses of sensitive information are described above. You have the right not to be retaliated against for exercising your privacy rights. We do not offer financial incentives or price or service differences in exchange for personal information.

edits.rationale: map_rights — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: How to submit a privacy request
after.body: To request access, deletion or correction, email privacy@democo.example or visit https://democo.example/privacy/requests. Tell us your request type and the email associated with your account; please do not send your password. You may submit a request without creating an account. We will acknowledge a request to know, delete or correct within 10 business days and ordinarily respond within 45 calendar days after receipt. If reasonably necessary, we may extend that period by up to 45 additional days and explain the reason within the first 45 days. If we cannot fulfill a request in whole or in part, we will explain the applicable basis and respond as the law requires.

edits.rationale: map_requests — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: How we verify requests
after.body: For an existing account, we generally ask you to authenticate using the account and may ask you to confirm the request through the account email. For a person who cannot access an account, we compare information you provide with records we already hold. We request only information reasonably necessary for verification in light of the request and information involved. We do not require you to create an account. If we cannot verify a request, we explain this and any available alternatives. We use information collected for verification only for verification, security or fraud prevention. We delete any new personal information collected for verification as soon as practical after processing your request, except records required by the applicable privacy-request recordkeeping rules.

edits.rationale: map_requests; map_supplement_privacy_request_verification_process — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Authorized agents
after.body: You may authorize an agent to make a request to know, delete or correct on your behalf through the same email address or request form. We may ask the agent for your signed permission, ask you to verify your identity directly with us, or ask you to confirm directly that you authorized the agent. We do not require you to resubmit the same request in your own name, and we do not require a power of attorney as the only way to use an agent. We do not require those additional authorization steps when an agent provides a valid power of attorney under California Probate Code sections 4121 through 4130.

edits.rationale: map_requests; map_supplement_privacy_request_verification_process — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Browser privacy signals
after.body: You can enable an opt-out preference signal such as Global Privacy Control in a supporting browser or extension. We do not sell or share personal information, including for accounts, devices, browser activity or offline activity, so receiving such a signal does not change a sale or sharing activity in our current service. We do not claim to provide a separate opt-out processing mechanism that we have not implemented. If our practices change, we will assess applicable opt-out and signal obligations before making that change.

edits.rationale: map_optout — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

before.heading: Policy updates
before.body: We may update this policy as our service changes. We will post the updated policy here.

after.heading: Policy updates
after.body: We review this policy at least annually and update it when our practices require a change. The last-updated date appears at the top of this policy. We post the current policy through a conspicuous Privacy link on the website and provide a printable version. We notify account holders by email before material changes to our information practices take effect.

edits.rationale: map_dates_access; map_supplement_material_policy_change_notice — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

CPPA

(f)  A business that uses or discloses a consumer’s sensitive personal information for purposes 
other than those specified in section 7027, subsection (m), shall provide a Notice of Right 
to Limit or the Alternative Opt-out Link in accordance with the CCPA and sections 7014 
and 7015. 
(g)  A business that offers a financial incentive or price or service difference shall provide a 
Notice of Financial Incentive in accordance with the CCPA and section 7016.  
Note: Authority cited: Section 1798.185, Civil Code. Reference: Sections 1798.100, 1798.105, 
1798.106, 1798.110, 1798.115, 1798.120, 1798.121, 1798.125, 1798.130, 1798.135, and 
1798.185, Civil Code. 
§ 7011.  Privacy Policy.  
(a) The purpose of the privacy policy is to provide consumers with a comprehensive 
description of a business’s online and offline information practices. It shall also inform 
consumers about the rights they have regarding their personal information and provide 
any information necessary for them to exercise those rights.  
(b) The privacy policy shall comply with section 7003, subsections (a) and (b).  
(c) The privacy policy shall be available in a format that allows a consumer to print it out as a 
document.  
(d) The privacy policy shall be posted online and accessible through a conspicuous link that 
complies with section 7003, subsections (c) and (d), using the word “privacy” on the 
business’s website homepage(s) or on the download or landing page of a mobile 
application. If the business has a California-specific description of consumers’ privacy 
rights on its website, then the privacy policy shall be included in that description. A 
business that does not operate a website shall make the privacy policy conspicuously 
available to consumers. A mobile application must also include a link to the privacy policy 
in the application’s settings menu.  
(e) The privacy policy shall include the following information: 
(1) A comprehensive description of the business’s online and offline information 
practices, which includes the following: 
(A) Identification of the categories of personal information the business has 
collected about consumers in the preceding 12 months. The categories shall be 
described using the specific terms set forth in Civil Code section 1798.140, 
subdivisions (v)(1)(A) – (K) and (ae)(1) – (2). To the extent that the business has 
discretion in its description, the business shall describe the category in a 
manner that provides consumers a meaningful understanding of the 
information being collected.

Tell us your request type and the email associated with your account; please do not send your password. You may submit a request without creating an account. We will acknowledge a request to know, delete or correct within 10 business days and ordinarily respond within 45 calendar days after receipt. If reasonably necessary, we may extend that period by up to 45 additional days and explain the reason within the first 45 days. If we cannot fulfill a request in whole or in part, we will explain the applicable basis and respond as the law requires.

edits.rationale: map_requests — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: How we verify requests
after.body: For an existing account, we generally ask you to authenticate using the account and may ask you to confirm the request through the account email. For a person who cannot access an account, we compare information you provide with records we already hold. We request only information reasonably necessary for verification in light of the request and information involved. We do not require you to create an account. If we cannot verify a request, we explain this and any available alternatives. We use information collected for verification only for verification, security or fraud prevention. We delete any new personal information collected for verification as soon as practical after processing your request, except records required by the applicable privacy-request recordkeeping rules.

edits.rationale: map_requests; map_supplement_privacy_request_verification_process — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Authorized agents
after.body: You may authorize an agent to make a request to know, delete or correct on your behalf through the same email address or request form. We may ask the agent for your signed permission, ask you to verify your identity directly with us, or ask you to confirm directly that you authorized the agent. We do not require you to resubmit the same request in your own name, and we do not require a power of attorney as the only way to use an agent. We do not require those additional authorization steps when an agent provides a valid power of attorney under California Probate Code sections 4121 through 4130.

edits.rationale: map_requests; map_supplement_privacy_request_verification_process — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

after.heading: Browser privacy signals
after.body: You can enable an opt-out preference signal such as Global Privacy Control in a supporting browser or extension. We do not sell or share personal information, including for accounts, devices, browser activity or offline activity, so receiving such a signal does not change a sale or sharing activity in our current service. We do not claim to provide a separate opt-out processing mechanism that we have not implemented. If our practices change, we will assess applicable opt-out and signal obligations before making that change.

edits.rationale: map_optout — T03 provision/fact mapping through T08 clause binding.

before.heading: Policy updates
before.body: We may update this policy as our service changes. We will post the updated policy here.

after.heading: Policy updates
after.body: We review this policy at least annually and update it when our practices require a change. The last-updated date appears at the top of this policy. We post the current policy through a conspicuous Privacy link on the website and provide a printable version. We notify account holders by email before material changes to our information practices take effect.

Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider, restricted first-party analytics service provider. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider. Retention: Declared city for account life plus 30 days; coarse IP-derived location 90 days.

Purposes: first-party event recommendations. Business-purpose recipients in that period: hosting service provider. Retention: Until preferences reset or account closure plus 30 days.

Sensitive personal information: account login and access credentials. Examples: account login combined with access credentials. Sources: consumer directly. Purposes: authenticate requested account, protect account security. Business-purpose recipients in that period: authentication service provider. Retention: Until credential rotation or account closure; revocable session credentials expire within 30 days.

clause.heading: Sources of information
clause.body: We collect account information, postal address, residence declarations, saved events and support messages directly from you. We collect identifiers, approximate location and usage information from your browser when you use our service. We derive music preferences from first-party interactions. We do not buy consumer information from data brokers.

clause.heading: Purposes for collection and use
clause.body: We use information for the category-specific purposes stated above. We also use identifiers to respond to support and assess privacy requirements that may apply to your residence declaration. We do not use event recommendations to make decisions about financial or lending services, housing, insurance, education, employment or healthcare.

clause.heading: Disclosures for business purposes in the preceding 12 months
clause.body: We disclosed each category listed in the information-practices section to its listed service-provider categories for the purposes stated there. These hosting, authentication, transactional email and restricted first-party analytics providers operate under contracts restricting their use to the permitted service. We have not otherwise disclosed these categories to third parties during the preceding 12 months.

clause.heading: Sale or sharing of personal information
clause.body: We have not sold personal information or shared it for cross-context behavioral advertising during the preceding 12 months, and we do not currently do either. We do not have actual knowledge that we sell or share personal information of consumers under 16. We do not use third-party advertising trackers or allow our providers to use consumer information for their own advertising.

clause.heading: Sensitive personal information
clause.body: We use and disclose account login credentials only as reasonably necessary to provide and secure the account service you request. We do not use or disclose sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those permitted by section 7027(m) of the California privacy regulations, and we do not use it to infer characteristics about you.

clause.heading: Retention
clause.body: The information-practices section states a period or criterion for each category. We keep support correspondence for 12 months after a request closes and records of privacy requests and our responses for at least 24 months. Documented legal holds may require limited information to be retained longer to meet a legal obligation, establish or defend a claim, or investigate a security incident. We restrict that information to the hold purpose and do not keep personal information longer than reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose.

clause.heading: California privacy rights
clause.body: California residents may ask us to know the personal information we have collected about them, including categories and specific pieces, sources, purposes, and categories of recipients; to delete personal information, subject to legal exceptions; and to correct inaccurate personal information. Where applicable, consumers may opt out of sale or sharing and limit certain uses or disclosures of sensitive personal information. Our current no-sale/no-sharing practices and limited account-security uses of sensitive information are described above. You have the right not to be retaliated against for exercising your privacy rights. We do not offer financial incentives or price or service differences in exchange for personal information.

(f)  A business that uses or discloses a consumer’s sensitive personal information for purposes 
other than those specified in section 7027, subsection (m), shall provide a Notice of Right 
to Limit or the Alternative Opt-out Link in accordance with the CCPA and sections 7014 
and 7015. 
(g)  A business that offers a financial incentive or price or service difference shall provide a 
Notice of Financial Incentive in accordance with the CCPA and section 7016.  
Note: Authority cited: Section 1798.185, Civil Code. Reference: Sections 1798.100, 1798.105, 
1798.106, 1798.110, 1798.115, 1798.120, 1798.121, 1798.125, 1798.130, 1798.135, and 
1798.185, Civil Code. 
§ 7011.  Privacy Policy.  
(a) The purpose of the privacy policy is to provide consumers with a comprehensive 
description of a business’s online and offline information practices. It shall also inform 
consumers about the rights they have regarding their personal information and provide 
any information necessary for them to exercise those rights.  
(b) The privacy policy shall comply with section 7003, subsections (a) and (b).  
(c) The privacy policy shall be available in a format that allows a consumer to print it out as a 
document.  
(d) The privacy policy shall be posted online and accessible through a conspicuous link that 
complies with section 7003, subsections (c) and (d), using the word “privacy” on the 
business’s website homepage(s) or on the download or landing page of a mobile 
application. If the business has a California-specific description of consumers’ privacy 
rights on its website, then the privacy policy shall be included in that description. A 
business that does not operate a website shall make the privacy policy conspicuously 
available to consumers. A mobile application must also include a link to the privacy policy 
in the application’s settings menu.  
(e) The privacy policy shall include the following information: 
(1) A comprehensive description of the business’s online and offline information 
practices, which includes the following: 
(A) Identification of the categories of personal information the business has 
collected about consumers in the preceding 12 months. The categories shall be 
described using the specific terms set forth in Civil Code section 1798.140, 
subdivisions (v)(1)(A) – (K) and (ae)(1) – (2). To the extent that the business has 
discretion in its description, the business shall describe the category in a 
manner that provides consumers a meaningful understanding of the 
information being collected.
